# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *Wuthering Heights* that had been on the shelf since the Clinton administration. Marion found it while shelving returns: a faint pencil mark beside a passage on page 212, where Heathcliff speaks. *Speech pattern inconsistent with earlier chapters,* the note read, in small, precise handwriting. *Compare p. 47.*

Marion held the book under the circulation desk lamp. The pencil was soft, the letters slanted slightly left, the kind of handwriting that belonged to someone who had learned cursive properly and then abandoned most of it. She checked the checkout card in the back—the library had gone digital years ago, but she still slid the old cards in as bookmarks out of habit. The last borrower was listed as R. Calloway.

She knew the name. Rowan Calloway ran the bait shop down by the harbor, the one with the hand-painted sign that said OPEN WHEN OPEN. He was maybe sixty, weathered, quiet in the way people became when they'd spent decades talking mostly to the sea. He came in every other Thursday, took out three or four books at a time, mostly classics, sometimes naval history. He never lingered
